transaction:
--------------
-- Synthetic disposable records only. The final rollback removes every write.
--------------

--------------
-- Run the entire file in ONE Workbench connection; do not commit halfway through.
--------------

--------------
SET @patient=CONCAT('sql-demo-',UUID())
--------------

--------------
SET @appointment=CONCAT('sql-demo-',UUID())
--------------

--------------
SET @token=CONCAT('sql-demo-',UUID())
--------------

--------------
SET @demo_date='2099-12-31'
--------------

--------------
START TRANSACTION
--------------

--------------
INSERT INTO users(id,name,role,metadata,createdAt,updatedAt)
VALUES (@patient,'Synthetic SQL demonstration','patient',JSON_OBJECT('synthetic',true),UTC_TIMESTAMP(3),UTC_TIMESTAMP(3))
--------------

--------------
INSERT INTO appointment_slots(doctorId,slotDate,slotMinute,bookedCount,capacity)
VALUES ('doc-1',@demo_date,480,1,1)
--------------

--------------
INSERT INTO appointments(id,patientId,doctorId,date,slotMinute,tokenNumber,status,priority,metadata,createdAt,updatedAt)
VALUES (@appointment,@patient,'doc-1',@demo_date,480,'SQL-DEMO','booked','normal',JSON_OBJECT('synthetic',true),UTC_TIMESTAMP(3),UTC_TIMESTAMP(3))
--------------

--------------
SET @seq=(SELECT COALESCE(MAX(tokenSeq),0)+1 FROM queue_tokens WHERE doctorId='doc-1' AND queueDate=@demo_date)
--------------

--------------
INSERT INTO queue_tokens(id,appointmentId,patientId,doctorId,queueDate,tokenSeq,tokenNumber,status,metadata,createdAt,updatedAt)
VALUES (@token,@appointment,@patient,'doc-1',@demo_date,@seq,'SQL-DEMO','waiting',JSON_OBJECT('synthetic',true),UTC_TIMESTAMP(3),UTC_TIMESTAMP(3))
--------------

--------------
SELECT a.id,a.status appointmentStatus,t.status tokenStatus,s.bookedCount
FROM appointments a JOIN queue_tokens t ON t.appointmentId=a.id
JOIN appointment_slots s ON s.doctorId=a.doctorId AND s.slotDate=a.date AND s.slotMinute=a.slotMinute WHERE a.id=@appointment
--------------

+-----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+
| id                                            | appointmentStatus | tokenStatus | bookedCount |
+-----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+
| sql-demo-6d6ce7f5-cb30-11f1-bd37-8a9f1a3da0b5 | booked            | waiting     |           1 |
+-----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+
--------------
UPDATE queue_tokens SET status='cancelled',updatedAt=UTC_TIMESTAMP(3) WHERE id=@token
--------------

--------------
-- AFTER UPDATE trigger synchronizes the appointment and releases the slot.
--------------

--------------
SELECT a.id,a.status appointmentStatus,t.status tokenStatus,s.bookedCount
FROM appointments a JOIN queue_tokens t ON t.appointmentId=a.id
JOIN appointment_slots s ON s.doctorId=a.doctorId AND s.slotDate=a.date AND s.slotMinute=a.slotMinute WHERE a.id=@appointment
--------------

+-----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+
| id                                            | appointmentStatus | tokenStatus | bookedCount |
+-----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+
| sql-demo-6d6ce7f5-cb30-11f1-bd37-8a9f1a3da0b5 | cancelled         | cancelled   |           0 |
+-----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+
--------------
SELECT action,actorId,details FROM audit_events WHERE entityId=@token ORDER BY timestamp
--------------

+----------------+------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| action         | actorId    | details                                                           |
+----------------+------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| created        | sql-client | {"status": "waiting", "queueDate": "2099-12-31"}                  |
| status_changed | sql-client | {"to": "cancelled", "from": "waiting", "queueDate": "2099-12-31"} |
+----------------+------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
--------------
ROLLBACK
--------------

--------------
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE id=@patient) remainingUsers,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE id=@appointment) remainingAppointments,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM queue_tokens WHERE id=@token) remainingTokens,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_events WHERE entityId=@token) remainingAuditEvents
--------------

+----------------+-----------------------+-----------------+----------------------+
| remainingUsers | remainingAppointments | remainingTokens | remainingAuditEvents |
+----------------+-----------------------+-----------------+----------------------+
|              0 |                     0 |               0 |                    0 |
+----------------+-----------------------+-----------------+----------------------+

columns.GENERATION_EXPRESSION: (case when (`status` in (_utf8mb4\'waiting\',_utf8mb4\'current\')) then `patientId` else NULL end)

checks.CHECK_CLAUSE: ((`servedAt` is null) or ((`calledAt` is not null) and (`servedAt` >= `calledAt`)))

testCases.name: directory joins specialty, clinic and normalized language with SQL ordering
SQL injection values cannot change search or select arbitrary sort expressions
empty search and out-of-range pages preserve a correct total
unauthenticated access and cross-clinic writes remain denied
simultaneous registrations cannot create two active visits for one patient
foreign keys reject orphan visits
emergency priority is selected by SQL before a normal token
database unique constraint prevents a second simultaneous consultation
patient queue responses conceal other patient identity
trigger records state changes and rejects reopening completed visits
pause is respected and the next call resumes correctly
appointment and token are created atomically with capacity accounting
capacity conflicts roll back without orphan appointments
cancellation trigger updates linked appointment and releases its slot
unique identities and optimistic profile versions prevent conflicting updates
a new conflicting identity cannot overwrite an existing account
staff appointment filters and SQL pagination use the assigned clinic
stored function, daily procedure, views and cursor return verifiable results
parameterized patient and appointment filters stay within the clinic
updated buffer capacity is used when an existing slot gains an opening
CHECK constraints reject negative fees and impossible slot occupancy
function returns NULL for missing, reversed and implausible timings
concurrent bookings from different patients cannot overfill the last slot
a booking submitted through the HTTP API is visible in SQL and cancels both records
